\chapter{Not Feeling Well}
\label{ch:ka-not-feeling-well}
\hlchaptermodality{82}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can say I am tired, have a cold, a cough or a headache, and that I need rest.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 82: i can say I am tired, have a cold, a cough or a headache, and that I need rest.

\section[āyāsa]{\kn{ಆಯಾಸ} (āyāsa) — tiredness}

\label{lesson:KA-C82-tiredness}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for fever, then the Kannada for pain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಆಯಾಸ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಆಯಾಸ}} (\emph{āyāsa}) — \textquotedblleft{}tiredness\textquotedblright{}, the heavy feeling at the end of a long day.

\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಆಯಾಸ} \kn{ಆಗಿದೆ}} (\emph{nanage āyāsa āgide}) — \textquotedblleft{}I am tired\textquotedblright{}, literally \textquotedblleft{}to me tiredness has happened\textquotedblright{}. The person sits in \textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ}}, \textquotedblleft{}to me\textquotedblright{}, the same way \textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಹಸಿವು}} says \textquotedblleft{}I am hungry\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A first word for how the body feels at the end of the day.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āyāsa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{āyāsa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nanage āyāsa āgide}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for fever, then the Kannada for pain, then say \emph{āyāsa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಆಯಾಸ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Tiredness\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[śīta]{\kn{ಶೀತ} (śīta) — a cold}

\label{lesson:KA-C82-cold}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for pain, then the Kannada for tiredness.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಶೀತ}}
\textbf{\kn{ಶೀತ}} (\emph{śīta}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cold\textquotedblright{}, the kind with a runny nose. The word also means \textquotedblleft{}cold, chill\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ಶೀತ} \kn{ಆಗಿದೆ}} (\emph{nanage śīta āgide}) — \textquotedblleft{}I have a cold\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An illness, said the same way as tiredness.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śīta}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{śīta}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nanage śīta āgide}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for pain, then the Kannada for tiredness, then say \emph{śīta} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಶೀತ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cold\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[kemmu]{\kn{ಕೆಮ್ಮು} (kemmu) — a cough}

\label{lesson:KA-C82-cough}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for tiredness, then the Kannada for a cold.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ಕೆಮ್ಮು}}
\textbf{\kn{ಕೆಮ್ಮು}} (\emph{kemmu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a cough\textquotedblright{}, and also the verb \textquotedblleft{}to cough\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ಕೆಮ್ಮು} \kn{ಇದೆ}} (\emph{kemmu ide}) — \textquotedblleft{}there is a cough\textquotedblright{}, the plain way to tell a doctor.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A second complaint for the doctor.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kemmu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kemmu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kemmu ide}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for tiredness, then the Kannada for a cold, then say \emph{kemmu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ಕೆಮ್ಮು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cough\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[talenōvu]{\kn{ತಲೆನೋವು} (talenōvu) — a headache}

\label{lesson:KA-C82-headache}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a cold, then the Kannada for a cough.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ತಲೆನೋವು}}
\textbf{\kn{ತಲೆನೋವು}} (\emph{talenōvu}) — \textquotedblleft{}a headache\textquotedblright{}. It is two words you already know, joined: \textbf{\kn{ತಲೆ}} (\emph{tale}), \textquotedblleft{}head\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\kn{ನೋವು}} (\emph{nōvu}), \textquotedblleft{}pain\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ನನಗೆ} \kn{ತಲೆನೋವು}} (\emph{nanage talenōvu}) — \textquotedblleft{}I have a headache\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Two known words make a new one: head + pain.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talenōvu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{talenōvu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{nanage talenōvu}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a cold, then the Kannada for a cough, then say \emph{talenōvu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ತಲೆನೋವು} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A headache\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[viśrānti]{\kn{ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ} (viśrānti) — rest}

\label{lesson:KA-C82-rest}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Kannada for a cough, then the Kannada for a headache.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \kn{ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ}}
\textbf{\kn{ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ}} (\emph{viśrānti}) — \textquotedblleft{}rest\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\kn{ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ} \kn{ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ}} (\emph{viśrānti tegedukoḷḷi}) — \textquotedblleft{}please take rest\textquotedblright{}, what you say to a friend who is unwell. The verb is \textbf{\kn{ತೆಗೆದುಕೊ}}, \textquotedblleft{}take\textquotedblright{}, which you already know.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
The answer to tiredness, a cold and a headache.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viśrānti}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{viśrānti}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} tell a friend \emph{viśrānti tegedukoḷḷi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Kannada for a cough, then the Kannada for a headache, then say \emph{viśrānti} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \kn{ವಿಶ್ರಾಂತಿ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Rest\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
